prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Produce exactly THREE equally wide TALL portrait Mars workshop backgrounds side by side as one landscape atlas, each portrait 390:844. Full edge-to-edge panels, straight cuts, no lines, frames, gutters, labels, text or UI. Input1 is the existing sunlit sheltered workcourt STYLE and geography; input2 equipment MATERIALS reference. Same cream prefab workshop wall and canopy, open red Mars beyond, fine dusty ochre working ground, realistic restrained retro industrial rendering. All fixed machinery and story details in UPPER 38%; LOWER 62% unobstructed QUIET ground. Important target centers stay within center 82% width of each panel. No people or loose tools/game objects.
LEFT: early workshop commissioning. At exactly x73%,y26% within panel, a substantial compact imported WORKSHOP PRESS fixed beneath canopy: cream factory hydraulic frame, dark vertical ram and clear horizontal work bed, stable floor mounting. It must be recognizably a press, not cupboards. Its usable press throat is centered x73%,y27%. Upper-left has only low bank of loose excavated regolith/spoil, unopened low service crate at far edge and empty ground; no assembled solar furnace, retort, gas plant or formed bricks. Locally fabricated structures have not appeared yet.
MIDDLE: same workshop much later making local iron. Preserve EXACT position, scale, camera and silhouette of the same press at RIGHT x73%,y26% and usable throat x73%,y27%—this target must line up identically across panels. At LEFT x27%,y28%, the completed imported electrolysis stack stands on SIMPLE bolted straight-steel support with TWO separate vertical cylindrical gas receivers and separate regulators; a distinct clean HYDROGEN service outlet faces camera on the left cylinder at x27%,y30%, opposite oxygen line stays separate and recedes away. A small established sunlit reflector and empty receiver are behind left edge, recognizable but subordinate. No fitted retort, reduced iron, local iron frame, methane reactor or cold propellant tanks yet. No complex locally machined fittings: stack/cylinders/controllers imported; supports made by one person with cut steel, bolts and spanners.
RIGHT: workshop after the dust storm. Same canopy, press remains unobtrusive at upper-right back, bright cleared sky returns. Center x50%,y28% is a fixed low CLEAN SERVICE BENCH with plain padded top and simple legs, broad receiving surface empty. At upper-left background, one previously installed photovoltaic rack is visibly coated in settled fine orange dust, distinct from the clean bench. No detached panel on bench, no wiping tool or cloth, no clean replacement solar rack; player brings actual array sections to bench. Dust lies on outside ground and canopy edges but service bench top is protected and clean. No duplicate machine inventory. The clearing should feel like familiar equipment awaiting maintenance, not wreckage.
Physical feasibility throughout: precision equipment imported, local fabrication only straight cut stock with ordinary bolted overlaps, folded sheet and plain supports, subtle hand-tool imperfections. No ornate custom lattice, cast furniture or glossy newly fabricated factory surfaces.
